w11: wdotool, wwmctl, wxprop, wxrandr, warandr and wmirror are on PATH.

  * On GNOME, the window commands need the bridge extension, and gnome-shell
    only scans extension directories at login: LOG OUT AND BACK IN ONCE.
  * /dev/uinput is now open to the user at the active seat (udev rule
    60-w11-uinput.rules).  Anyone who can open it can type as you.
  * On an X11 session the tools hand over to the real ones:
    pacman -S xdotool wmctrl xorg-xprop xorg-xrandr

w11: wdotool, wwmctl, wxprop, wxrandr, warandr and wmirror are on PATH.

  * On GNOME, the window commands need the bridge extension, and gnome-shell
    only scans extension directories at login: LOG OUT AND BACK IN ONCE.
  * /dev/uinput is now open to the user at the active seat (udev rule
    60-w11-uinput.rules).  Anyone who can open it can type as you.
  * On an X11 session the tools hand over to the real ones:
    pacman -S xdotool wmctrl xorg-xprop xorg-xrandr

Optional dependencies for w11
    python-gobject: the warandr GUI [installed]
    gtk3: the warandr GUI [installed]
    wl-mirror: wmirror, region and odd-shape mirroring on wlroots [installed]
    gnome-shell: the bridge extension, needed by the window commands on GNOME
    xdotool: the real tool wdotool hands over to, on X11 and through xw11 [installed]
    wmctrl: the real tool wwmctl hands over to, on X11 and through xw11 [installed]
    xorg-xprop: the real tool wxprop hands over to, on X11 and through xw11 [installed]
    xorg-xrandr: the real tool wxrandr hands over to, on X11 and through xw11 [installed]
